\section*{Question 3}

An object moving along a curve in the \(x y\)-plane has position \((x(t), y(t))\) at time \(t \geq 0\) with \(\frac{d x}{d t}=3+\cos \left(t^{2}\right)\). The derivative \(\frac{d y}{d t}\) is not explicitly given. At time \(t=2\), the object is at position (1, 8).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Find the \(x\)-coordinate of the position of the object at time \(t=4\).
\item[(b)] At time \(t=2\), the value of \(\frac{d y}{d t}\) is -7 . Write an equation for the line tangent to the curve at the point \((x(2), y(2))\).
\item[(c)] Find the speed of the object at time \(t=2\).
\item[(d)] For \(t \geq 3\), the line tangent to the curve at \((x(t), y(t))\) has a slope of \(2 t+1\). Find the acceleration vector of the object at time \(t=4\).
\item[(a)]
\[
\begin{aligned}
x(4) & =x(2)+\int_{2}^{4}\left(3+\cos \left(t^{2}\right)\right) d t \\
& =1+\int_{2}^{4}\left(3+\cos \left(t^{2}\right)\right) d t=7.132 \text { or } 7.133
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(b)]
\[
\begin{aligned}
& \left.\frac{d y}{d x}\right|_{t=2}=\left.\frac{\frac{d y}{d t}}{\frac{d x}{d t}}\right|_{t=2}=\frac{-7}{3+\cos 4}=-2.983 \\
& y-8=-2.983(x-1)
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(c)] The speed of the object at time \(t=2\) is
\[
\sqrt{\left(x^{\prime}(2)\right)^{2}+\left(y^{\prime}(2)\right)^{2}}=7.382 \text { or } 7.383 .
\]
\item[(d)]
\[
\begin{aligned}
& x^{\prime \prime}(4)=2.303 \\
& y^{\prime}(t)=\frac{d y}{d t}=\frac{d y}{d x} \cdot \frac{d x}{d t}=(2 t+1)\left(3+\cos \left(t^{2}\right)\right) \\
& y^{\prime \prime}(4)=24.813 \text { or } 24.814
\end{aligned}
\]
The acceleration vector at \(t=4\) is
\[
\langle 2.303,24.813\rangle \text { or }\langle 2.303,24.814\rangle \text {. }
\]
\end{itemize}
\[
3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}
1: \int_{2}^{4}\left(3+\cos \left(t^{2}\right)\right) d t \\
1: \text { handles initial condition } \\
1: \text { answer }
\end{array}\right.
\]
\(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { finds }\left.\frac{d y}{d x}\right|_{t=2} \\ 1: \text { equation }\end{array}\right.\)
1 : answer
\(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: x^{\prime \prime}(4) \\ 1: \frac{d y}{d t} \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
